# Charter — S20 Eval Hillclimb (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

- **Project:** S20 'Eval hillclimb', track v1, ADM phase G, delivery plateau, tranche 9, plan `docs/plans/slices/S20-eval-hillclimb.md`. The record's only linked issue is #14, which is closed.
- **Sponsor:** the programme's sponsoring group, through the tranche-9 PI plan and the standing delegation 01a1ff1f-e4ba-72dc-9c1a-13049933cf14. Tranche 9's authorisation is not this pack's to give; the P0 package `project_in_unauthorised_tranche:S20` clears only on that authorisation.
- **Objective:** the `eval-hillclimb` and `cost-hillclimb` methods become a loop over one eval — a goal, a stopping condition, a fixed train/test split drawn once by S19, and rounds that each propose a change, run the full set, and are kept or reverted on the held-out number. The climb ends with the winning version named, a per-round train/test table, a paired delta with a significance test, two before/after transcript pairs, and failures classified by cause rather than blamed on the model.
- **Scope in:** `eval_climb` state; `eval_climbs.start/get/list/round/compare/stop`; `eval_runs.regrade`; the `eval_climb.changed` and `eval_climb.round_completed` events; the one new job kind `eval.regrade`; the stall-triage round; the cost-search goal; the final report.
- **Scope out:** any UI — screen 21 is declared for S12; a second model runtime (the analyzer is an agent principal over `/mcp` or a person writing `change.md`); automatic application of a change to production code; editing an eval mid-climb; a second McNemar.
- **Retrospective status:** the project row is closed and measured built, while its closure review, change control, baseline, WBS, registers, contract, Phase-G review and artefact set were never published. This pack is authored on 2026-11-28 to supply the lifecycle record; it does not attest a contemporaneous ceremonial review, and it claims no retired gate command ran.

soaw.title: Statement of Architecture Work — S20 Eval Hillclimb (retrospective, 2026-11-28)

body.assignment: The architecture work assigns S20 the hillclimb loop the eval and benchmark surface must carry: one `eval_climb` state per climb, six `eval_climbs.*` actions plus `eval_runs.regrade`, two events, the stall-triage round, the cost-search goal and the final report. This statement governs the retrospective record of a project the record marks closed and measured built, read at the 2026-11-28 snapshot under the standing delegation.
body.scope: In scope are `migrations/0029_s20_eval_climb_report.sql`, `crates/domain/src/eval/climb.rs` (the loop state machine, the keep/revert rule, the bucket vocabulary and the stopping predicate), `crates/store/src/eval/climb.rs`, `crates/actions/src/eval/climbs.rs`, the registry `EXPECTED` array and one `parity_http_mcp` sample per action. Out of scope are any UI, a second runtime, a second McNemar, mid-climb edits to an eval, its cases or its metrics, and any automatic application of a winning change to production code.
body.responsibilities: The programme architect authors this retrospective statement; the delivery team is accountable for the tree and its suites; the Architecture Board reviews the artefact set; the SRO accepts the project's closure at the tranche-9 review. The eval owner is consulted because the goal, the stopping condition and the plan sign-off are theirs, and the analyzer principal is the consumer the round action must serve without ever letting it set its own budget.
body.acceptance_criteria: The plan's §7 gate names the acceptance: the schema suite proves one table RLS-forced and no spend column; the gate suite proves a climb cannot redraw S19's split and that no round runs before the plan is signed; the regrade suite proves a grader fix lands in a new run; the compare suite proves refusal across versions, graders or splits; the domain rules suite proves the keep/revert rules; the stall suite proves a fourth content round is refused; the cost suite proves no round without registered gates; the final suite proves the report names the winner; and the served lock check holds. The record carries the project as measured built; the gate's commands are `rbuild` invocations, and `rbuild` was retired by the owner on 2026-11-20, so this statement claims no run of them.
body.contract: The contract is the delivery contract this pack carries: one `eval_climb` row per climb with spend read as a sum over `eval_case_result.usage` rather than a maintained column; the split owned by S19's version and not redrawable by the climb; `eval_climbs.start` and `stop` behind `evals:approve` while `round` needs only `evals:write`; and the winning change applied only by a person's ordinary `procedures.update`.
body.retrospective: This statement is authored on 2026-11-28 for the tranche-9 rework. No contemporaneous statement of architecture work exists; the delivery was recorded in the slice plan, its migration and its suites. The statement records what the plan, the record and the tree show today, and it states plainly that the plan's §7 gate text still names `rbuild --gate`, a command the owner retired on 2026-11-20 in favour of the repository's GitHub-hosted preflight workflow for the compile and lint verdict.

# Inception Analysis — S20 Eval hillclimb (retrospective, Phase G)

## Current state

Before S20 the hillclimb was a person editing an eval, rerunning it and reading a number with no held-out discipline: nothing proposed a change, nothing kept or reverted it, and a stall produced another pass rather than a diagnosis. At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the project row 01a1d039-0d31-7d0f-ab1f-16240952e223 is closed and measured built, and the tree carries the migration, the three modules and the eight suites; this analysis is authored retrospectively for phase G, not as a contemporaneous inception.

## Reuse sources

The slice plan's §4 names what the climb reuses: the eval-hillclimb method for the wall, the stopping rules, the bucket vocabulary and the revert rules verbatim; the cost-hillclimb method for the search order and the rule that adoption gates are registered before round 1; the audit method's arithmetic for the noise floor against the headroom; the benchmark slice's exact McNemar, called rather than copied; and the eval runner's tables, case runner, four grader kinds, report and fixed split with its digest.

## Build vs reuse

Reuse the eval runner's tick, split, report and usage rows, and the benchmark's exact test; build only one climb state, six climb actions, one regrade action, two events and one job kind. Refused: a conveyor-hosted model loop, a second McNemar, any UI, automatic application of a winning change, and a maintained spend column. The build therefore adds one DDL statement — eval_climb.narrative_md in migrations/0029_s20_eval_climb_report.sql — to tables the eval runner already owns.

## Risks

Four traps shape the design. A split chosen by score destroys the held-out signal, so the climb cannot redraw it. An analyzer that reads test transcripts overfits the number it reports, so the round records the transcript ids it was handed. A change inside the noise floor makes keep or revert a coin flip, so delta is set from the measured floor. A maintained spend counter drifts from the rows it counts, so spend is summed at read time. Each has a named suite, and the record's 5 open packages are named rather than waived.

# Architecture Analysis — S20 Eval hillclimb (retrospective, Phase G)

## Current state

The eval runner already ships eval, eval_version, eval_case, eval_metric, eval_runs with variant, round, change_md, change_patch, summary and narrative_md, the case runner, four grader kinds, the report with mean, CI, noise floor and cost, and a split drawn once with a digest. It has no notion of a proposed change and no keep or revert rule. S20 adds exactly that layer: one climb state, a round protocol on the existing tick, comparison, stall triage, a cost goal and a final report.

## Options considered

Three options were weighed. A conveyor-hosted model loop that proposes and applies changes was rejected: the slice plan fixes that a round returns to the caller, and the analyzer is an agent over /mcp or a person writing change_md. One round as an eval_run row under the existing tick was chosen, so the climb inherits the runner's reaper and adds no second driver. Redrawing the split per climb was rejected, because a climb that can move the split has no held-out number to report.

## Risks

The four named traps are the score-chosen split, analyzer access to test transcripts, a change below the noise floor and a maintained spend counter; a fifth is comparing a regraded run against an old one without regrading every variant. The schema, gate, stall and compare suites carry the checks. On the record, the P0 project_in_unauthorised_tranche:S20 clears only on tranche authorisation, so this pack can resolve the P1 closure packages but cannot make the tranche decision.

## Dependency map

The climb depends inward on the eval runner for its tables, tick and split, and on the benchmark slice for the exact McNemar, called not copied; it depends outward on the screens slice, which owns the hillclimb screen's read model. The record's only linked issue #14 is closed. Inside the pack the order is climb state, actions, round, compare, stall triage, cost goal and final report, which is the order the eight suites exercise.

documents.body:
# Architecture Design — S20 Eval hillclimb (retrospective, Phase G)

## Context and boundary

The design owns the climb state, the round protocol, comparison, stall triage, cost search and the final report; it must not duplicate the eval runner's tables, tick or split, the benchmark's exact test, or the screens slice's UI. The boundary is one eval_climb row per climb with spend summed at read time, and a winner applied only by a person's ordinary procedure update, never by the climb itself.

## Aggregates, tables and actions

eval_climb is the aggregate: goal jsonb, direction, reps, stopping, plateau_k, delta, cost_ceiling_cents, current_round, best_round, best_test_score, approve_each_round, off_limits and status. The only new DDL is eval_climb.narrative_md in migrations/0029_s20_eval_climb_report.sql. A round is an eval_runs row with variant v<N>, round, change_md, change_patch, prediction and summary.suspicious. The actions are eval_climbs.start, get, list, round, compare and stop plus eval_runs.regrade; the events are eval_climb.changed and eval_climb.round_completed; the one new job kind is eval.regrade.

## Decisions

A round returns to the caller. The split belongs to the eval runner's version and cannot be redrawn. Comparison calls the benchmark's exact McNemar. Stall triage is a round, not advice. Cost search is a goal, not a mode of the loop. start and stop need evals:approve while round needs only evals:write. Applying the winner is a person's action. Each decision has a refusal in the gate, stall, cost or compare suite, so none of them rests on prose alone.

## Acceptance

The acceptance set is the eight suites the tree carries — eval_climb_schema, eval_climb_rules, eval_climb_gate, eval_compare, eval_regrade, eval_stall, eval_cost_walk and eval_final — plus the served lock check. The schema suite proves one RLS-forced table and no spend column; the gate suite proves a climb cannot redraw the split and that no round runs before the plan is signed; the stall suite proves a fourth content round is refused.

## Architecture artefacts

The pack carries the seven Phase A–D artefacts: Stakeholder Map, Driver/Goal/Objective Catalog, Requirements Catalog and Solution Concept Diagram at phase a on the psa plateau; Business Capability Map at phase b; Data Entity/Data Component Catalog at phase c; and Technology Standards Catalog at phase d. The Architecture Artefact Index documents their titles and links. All are authored on 2026-11-28 for this retrospective phase-G record.

## Assignment

The assignment is recorded retrospectively. # User stories — S20 Eval hillclimb (retrospective, Phase G)

## Personas

An eval owner sets the goal, the stopping condition and the plan sign-off; an analyzer principal, an agent over /mcp or a person, proposes one change per round; and a reviewer reads a winner with its held-out evidence attached. All three act through the same actions, and none of them — not the analyzer and not the reviewer — may set the climb's budget or move its split.

## Stories

As an eval owner, I want a signed plan carrying the goal, the will/won't-change table and the stopping condition, so that no round begins before the method's terms are fixed. As an analyzer, I want one round action that takes change_md, an optional patch and a falsifiable prediction, so that each change is one attributable hypothesis. As a reviewer, I want the climb to end with a per-round train/test table and a paired significance test, so that the winner is named by evidence rather than by memory.

## Scenarios

Given a climb whose plan is signed, when the first round is submitted, then it is queued as an eval_run row and no second job kind is created. Given two consecutive flat test deltas, when another content round is proposed, then it is refused until a five-bucket categorisation is supplied. Given a grader fix, when the regrade action runs, then a new run is written under the eval's current version and the comparison is re-run, never compared against the old scale.

## Verify

The gate suite proves the plan sign-off and the immovable split; the stall suite proves a fourth content round is refused; the regrade suite proves the new run is written and never in place; the compare suite proves a refusal across versions, graders or splits; the domain rules suite proves the keep or revert table; the cost suite proves no round runs without registered gates; and the final suite proves the report names the winner.

risk.title: A split redrawn by score destroys the held-out signal
risk.body: Hand-picking the worst cases for train guarantees regression to the mean and a flat test set. S19 draws the split and locks it with a digest; a climb that could redraw it would have no held-out signal at all. The plan's §8 trap 1 is the statement of this risk, and the gate suite's a_climb_cannot_redraw_the_split is the check.
risk.response: Attempt a redraw in the gate suite before any change to the climb's read path; a climb that can move the split is a defect of the action, never a convenience.

risk.title: The analyzer reads test transcripts and the round overfits the number it reports
risk.body: The wall is data access, not an instruction: a round whose proposal cites a test transcript is void. If the transcript ids the analyzer was handed are not recorded, a round can quietly read the held-out set and the climb reports a number it trained on. The plan's §8 trap 2 names this and requires the ids to be recorded.
risk.response: Record the handed transcript ids on every round and refuse a round whose proposal cites one that belongs to the test side; read the record after any round whose gain is surprising.

risk.title: A change smaller than the noise floor makes keep or revert a coin flip
risk.body: If the best case for a change sits inside the measured noise floor, the keep or revert decision is decided by chance and a full pass is spent learning nothing. The plan's §8 trap 3 requires delta to be set from the measured floor and a proposed change predicting a smaller gain to be refused with the number.
risk.response: Read the climb's delta against S19's noise floor before round 1 and refuse a round whose prediction is inside the band; treat a kept round inside the band as a measurement defect.

risk.title: A maintained spend counter would drift from the rows it counts
risk.body: Spend is deliberately not a column on eval_climb: it is a sum over the climb's eval_case_result.usage at read time, because a maintained counter is the one thing that can drift from the rows it counts. A future refactor that adds a spend column would reintroduce that drift, and the schema suite's no_climb_spend_column is the guard.
risk.response: Read the schema suite before any change to the climb's read model; a spend column is refused as a defect of the table, not accepted as a convenience.

issue.title: The row is closed with no closure review and an empty closure-outputs declaration
issue.body: At the 2026-11-28 snapshot the project row records status closed and measured built while meta.closure_outputs is empty and no closure review exists for S20.
